utterances.text: I apologise, but does that mean an additional three assistants or that -- does that include the warrant officer or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: No, normally throughout my three years there, there would be two of us who would actually go out and work and we would have a secretary who would remain in Belgrade, which is very standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, since you worked for the Ministry of Defence, did you personally, from your Belgrade office, send reports to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: Yes. As I've indicated to the Court, my boss in Belgrade was the ambassador, initially Ambassador Roberts and then Ambassador Donnelly. And I worked as part of his diplomatic team assigned to former Yugoslavia, which again is very normal behaviour in any country in which we have an embassy which has a defence or military attache included within its diplomatic staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, please provide me a direct answer to the following question: Did you as military attache personally send reports to the Ministry of Defence of Great Britain?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: I apologise if I didn't make it clear. I sent my reports through my ambassador, as part of his team, to the Ministry of Defence, and that is perfectly standard procedure throughout the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible, I ask that we now show 65 ter exhibit number or document number 00688. It was used today, but I think it wasn't assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This, Your Honours, is identified as P01404.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, it's page 1 in my version, and it says: "Summary." Who is the author of this summary?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: At the top of the reports, Your Honours, it says from Britmilrep which is signal slang for British military representative Belgrade, therefore that would be coming from myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell me whether this entire report, dated the 13th of May, 1998, is it all authored by you or does it include parts drafted by the ambassador?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, Your Honours, I can only see page 1 so I can't make a complete comment on this report. But as I indicated to the Court earlier, my job as a military or defence attache was to input my thoughts on the military situation in Kosovo as I saw it nearly on a day-to-day basis during 1998 and 1999. And my ambassador or the deputy ambassador, as again I have indicated to the Court, would add any political comment that he thought was relevant to the situation. So you could say it is a joint report as part of a team reporting on a very complex situation that developed throughout 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I should like to observe another thing. It is of the essence for me for you to tell me what is your direct knowledge of things and what is the knowledge that you obtained from some other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if the usher could bring up the first page of this document in the English language on the screen, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From the reply which you have just given me, one could not ascertain what is it that is authorised by you and what is it that was authorised by the ambassador or an assistant of his or a third person. So please take a look at page 1 of this telegram. Can you tell me what information in it was contributed by you and what was imparted by some other persons?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: On page 1, I would suspect that, bearing in mind this is nearly 12 years ago, that the majority of that information on page 1 and page 2 was contributed by me since it concerns military activity. But as I've tried to make it clear, I was working as part of a team to my ambassador in an attempt to represent and report as accurately as possible. And from some of these reports, as you are well aware, I would have conversations through the FLS as to the situation that was in general deteriorating in the province of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. But still one thing is not clear to me. Who bears responsibility for the content of the telegram sent by the ambassador to the Ministry of Defence and signs it if all of this is your report and there are no interventions in it whatsoever by the ambassador and it is sent and signed by him, this telegram, that is?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: So, as I've indicated, there is a seamless transition between the ambassador, who is head of the team, diplomatic team, in Belgrade, of which I am part of his team. I have made the military content in this particular telegram, and the ambassador as the head of the overall team in Belgrade will sign it off, which I think you'll find is completely normal procedure in all our embassies throughout the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, Colonel: On the 13th of May, 1998, were you in Kosovo and Metohija or were you in Belgrade on that date?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: The report is of the two days that I was in Kosovo on the 11th/12th of May. The report was probably put together on our return to Belgrade, dated the 13th of May. I would have made notes on either an automatic recorder or in my own notebook, and then on return to Belgrade, I would have drafted a report which the ambassador or his deputy would have seen. And then that report would have been sent to various people, the Ministry of Defence included, as normal standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see Exhibit P01404, that is a report from the 28th of May, 1998. It was on the 65 ter list under number 00687. 1405.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this is a report, if I'm right, and if I'm not, please correct me, of the 28th of May, 1998. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: That is the date of the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You stated that you personally witnessed the events which are described in this report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me when was this report drawn up?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: Well, as you see at the bottom of the report, day one was the 26th of May, and it's a two-day tour of western Kosovo so we would have been touring on the 26th/27th of May, and the report, as I've mentioned already to you, sir, would have probably been written as dated on the 28th of May, when we returned to Belgrade. Sometimes I would have sent this by various means back to Belgrade and continued staying in Kosovo. So that might help you understand the fact that there are the gaps between when the tour took place, the visit, and the actual report being sent back to the Ministry of Defence and other person -- and other agencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is time we adjourned for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. We do need to adjourn now because of a Plenary meeting of all the Judges. Before we adjourn, could I mention that there has been received today a motion of the Prosecution concerning Witness K87, and it proposes the use of Rule 92 quater. As we understand that that is the one remaining witness, we need to deal with that matter expeditiously. And the Chamber would propose to receive oral submissions both from Prosecution and Defence about the matter at the end of the evidence of the present witness, Mr. Crosland, whenever that may be, tomorrow or Wednesday. We will adjourn now and resume at 9.00 in the morning, and the screens will be closed for the witness to leave. Tomorrow morning at 9.00, Mr. Crosland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of October, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.48 p.m.,
